data.title: Hyperbeat Launches USD+ Stablecoin for Risk-Adjusted Yield Across Hyperliquid
data.description:
Hyperbeat, a native yield layer in the Hyperliquid ecosystem, has launched USD+, a stablecoin product that offers risk-adjusted yield across the ecosystem. According to Foresight News, USD+ allocates funds across Morpho markets, HyperLend, Hyperliquid Earn USDC, Liquid Bank credit markets, and delta-neutral strategies.

Users can use USD+ as collateral in Liquid Banking to borrow up to 85% of its value while continuing to earn yield, with borrowed funds available for trading, spending, or withdrawal. Hyperbeat also introduced Builder Codes to support native integration of USD+ into front ends.

data.title: Ethereum Spot ETFs See $131M Net Outflow, Led by BlackRock’s ETHA
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing RootData, U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $131 million in net outflows yesterday, November 19 (U.S. Eastern Time). BlackRock’s ETHA led with $124 million in outflows, followed by Grayscale’s ETHE with $5.2 million.

data.title: Bubblemaps Says Crypto KOL Daumen Made About $340,000 Using Linked Wallets Around Token Calls
data.description:
Bubblemaps said crypto KOL Daumen traded more than 5,000 tokens alongside his public wallet through nine linked wallets since April, with linked-wallet activity involving 760 tokens. According to Foresight News, the wallets often bought in the same block, after which Daumen posted calls that pushed prices up; the linked wallets sold first, followed by his public wallet.

The linked wallets reportedly made about $340,000 across those 760 tokens, while the public wallet earned about $50,000. Bubblemaps also said the public wallet funded a deployment address associated with a developer who has launched more than 400 tokens since October and quickly sold them.

data.title: Moody’s Downgrades Nvidia’s Credit Outlook From Positive to Stable
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing Chang'an Jie Zhi Shi, Moody’s Ratings lowered Nvidia’s credit outlook from positive to stable, citing governance concerns following the departure of longtime CEO Jensen Huang; the Global Times reported the move on November 19, citing Bloomberg. Moody’s said an upgrade was unlikely within the next 12 to 18 months, and its analysts said Huang’s departure had added uncertainty to Nvidia’s business strategy and financial policies. The agency’s outlook categories are positive, stable, negative and developing.

Nvidia announced on November 12 that its board had approved Huang’s resignation as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. On November 17, Huang said in his first public statement since stepping down that he would be willing to return as CEO if invited by the board. The board chair said on November 18 that the company did not plan to reinstate him and would consider internal and external candidates. Interim CEO Colette Kress told a companywide meeting on Wednesday, “Let’s look forward.”

The report said executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles, tasked by Nvidia’s board with finding a new president, had contacted Arm CEO Rene Haas about the position. Other candidates reportedly include Nvidia Vice President Ian Buck, AMD CEO Lisa Su and Apple Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji.

On November 20 (UTC+8), Nvidia shares fell to an intraday low of $145.74 and closed at $145.98, giving the company a market capitalization of $3.52 trillion. The stock fell for a sixth straight session, erasing about $668.8 billion in market value, equivalent to approximately RMB 4.46197 trillion. Since the events involving Huang began, Nvidia shares have fallen nearly 31.7%, erasing about $1.63 trillion in market value, or approximately RMB 10.95 trillion.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | USCC Says Beijing Seeks Industry Advantage Amid US-China Trade Tensions
data.description: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission’s annual report examines economic, technology and national security challenges posed by China. Chair Randy Schriver and Vice-Chair Mike Kuiken said Beijing continues to seek an advantage over the US in many industries globally despite increased dialogue between the countries’ leaders, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | Japan's Top Property Insurers Report Cyber Claim Surge
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Japan's largest property insurers are reporting a sharp rise in cyber insurance claims as AI-driven attacks grow more sophisticated and hacking incidents surge nationwide.

data.title: Indian Rupee Breaks Above 93 Against the Dollar for First Time Since April, Gains 0.3%
data.description: According to Jin10, the Indian rupee rose above 93 against the U.S. dollar for the first time since April, gaining 0.3% from the previous close.

data.description: Royal Bank of Canada increased its holdings in Bitcoin treasury company Strive by 58%. According to Odaily, Bitcoin Treasuries said on X that the bank disclosed a total position of 74,035 shares, valued at $1.2 million.

data.title: Yen Leads G-10 Currencies as Tech Rout Spurs Haven Demand
data.description: According to Bloomberg, the yen led gains among Group of 10 currencies on Friday as investors sought havens amid a deepening selloff in technology stocks that spread to Asia trading.

data.title: AI | Malaysia Exports Set October Record on AI-Related Demand
data.description: Malaysia’s exports reached a record high in October, growing at their fastest pace in more than five years amid sustained demand for AI-related products, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Pakistan Minister Visits India for Regional Forum, First High-Level Trip Since 2023
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Pakistan Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi Friday for a two-day regional forum, marking the first high-level visit of its kind since 2023. The visit does not signal a broader thaw in ties between the neighbors.

data.title: Treasuries Near Longest Rally in Almost Five Months as Haven Demand Rises
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Treasuries are on course for their longest rally in almost five months as mounting doubts about the artificial intelligence trade deepen a global stock selloff and drive investors toward haven assets.

data.title: PBOC Keeps Yuan Fix Steady After Volatility Rises Following APEC
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China’s central bank set a largely steady yuan fixing Friday, signaling it wants to curb sharp currency moves. The yuan posted its biggest drop since March after a trilateral leaders’ meeting.

data.title: Malaysia's Export Growth Hits a Five-and-a-Half-Year High
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Malaysia's exports grew 61.1% year over year in October to 239.2 billion ringgit, equivalent to $58.16 billion, driven by strong demand for electrical and electronic products. The country's Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said the increase was faster than September's 54.5% growth and the strongest since April 2021.

Imports rose 54.4% year over year to 197.41 billion ringgit, leaving a trade surplus of 41.79 billion ringgit, up from 34.35 billion ringgit in September.

Manufactured goods accounted for 89% of October exports and grew 68% year over year. Electrical and electronic products made up about 52.5% of exports and increased 87.2%. Month over month, exports rose 10.9% and imports gained 8.8%.

data.title: India Plans New Bond Derivatives Trading Platform by Year-End
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, people familiar with the matter said India’s sovereign bond clearing institution plans to launch a new trading platform for bond forwards by the end of December. India Clearing Corporation Limited (CCIL) will introduce a request-for-quote platform that allows bilateral trading and enables companies to price securities through a centralized venue, one person said. The person requested anonymity because the discussions are not public.

Indian insurers widely use bond forwards to hedge against interest-rate fluctuations. CCIL data show that the total notional value of these transactions has reached 1.1 trillion rupees, or about $12 billion, so far this year.

data.title: ING Group: Strong AI Exports Could Put the Won and Taiwan Dollar Among Asia’s Leaders
data.description: According to Jin10, ING Group Chief Economist Deepali Bhargava said lower oil prices and a weaker U.S. dollar would support Asian currencies. ING Group favors the South Korean won and Taiwan dollar, citing strong AI-related exports, large current-account surpluses, and rising demand from exporters converting foreign-currency earnings into local currencies. ING Group expects the U.S. dollar to fall to 1,275 won and 31.5 Taiwan dollars by the end of 2027. It also expects the Singapore dollar to remain relatively strong in 2027, with the U.S. dollar falling to 1.26 Singapore dollars by the end of the year.

data.title: Citi Raises Pinduoduo Price Target to $143 From $136
data.description: According to Jin10, Citi raised its price target for Pinduoduo (PDD.O) to $143 from $136.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Saxo Bank: Anthropic’s High Valuation Faces a Test
data.description: According to Jin10, Saxo Bank Chief Investment Strategist Charu Chanana said in a research report that Anthropic faces challenges in sustaining its high valuation despite a successful IPO debut. Its share price retreated from its opening high and weakened further after hours, suggesting investors have begun distinguishing AI-driven market enthusiasm from the economics of delivering AI services. Anthropic’s pricing power may not last. As competition intensifies and token prices continue to fall, the company could face an “unsettling mismatch”: revenue depends on user activity and pricing, while infrastructure costs were committed years ago and are difficult to adjust.

data.title: U.S. Dollar Holds Near 19-Month High as Safe-Haven Demand Rises
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, the U.S. Dollar Index hovered around 103.9, its highest level since April 2025, while the dollar remained near a 19-month high. Unease over the AI boom has pushed investors toward safe-haven assets. Markets expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates by 25 basis points in December, while a larger increase remains possible.

data.title: Creditors Seek to Block SpaceX From Sending $40 Billion in Chips Into Orbit
data.description: According to Jin10, the Financial Times reported that creditors are seeking to block SpaceX from putting chips worth $40 billion into orbit.
